evidence.location: section 4, VG3 criteria row, VG3-C7 ("a model without the mode, with or without includes, gives byte-identical `gnd validate` output (R0.3); one case is an include root without the mode"), read with section 5, Compatibility
evidence.observation: VG3-C7 is universally quantified ("a model without the mode, with or without includes, gives byte-identical `gnd validate` output"), but the evidence 003-phase-VG3.md cites is T7 over tests/fixtures/vg3/base-outputs.json, whose 8 non-h30 outputs (cases built in tests/vg3_cases.py:106-124: seed-alone, seed-alone-document, include-root-without-mode, include-root-without-mode-document, each text and json) are all valid models with no span or rule issue on an included element. Two shipped VG3 changes are not mode-gated: src/gnd/commands/checking.py:91 now routes every `--document` span-walk issue through remap_issues (the H37 fix this plan's section 2 states without a mode qualifier: "So do the diagnostics of the span walk, which bypass the remapping step today (H37)"), and remap_issues (src/gnd/model/_includes.py:290-325) since VG3 also maps `$.object_types[id=…]` selectors (H17: "Diagnostics on included object types gain the `includes[ID]:` prefix"). So an include root WITHOUT the unattended mode whose `--document` walk raises an issue on an included element (e.g. an excerpt mismatch) changes its issue path from `$.object_types[id=work].provenance.spans[0]` to `includes[seed]:$.object_types[id=work]…` relative to the pre-VG3 base, yet section 5 names the prefix change only for unattended roots ("the address of the issue gains the `includes[ID]:` prefix (H37, VG3-C11)") and says of VG3 (a) that it "admit[s] inputs that 0.4.0 refuses and refuse nothing 0.4.0 admits" without naming this byte-level change for non-unattended include roots.

concerns.recommendation: Either add one refusal case to the vg3 base-output fixture (a non-unattended include root with a span issue on an included element, text and json) so VG3-C7's universal form is pinned, or record in section 5 / the close bundle that the H17/H37 remapping also changes issue paths on refused include roots without the mode, aligning the documented format promise with the compatibility accounting.
concerns.title: VG3-C7's byte-identical claim is sampled only over valid models; the H17/H37 remapping also changes issue paths on refused include roots without the unattended mode

summary: Read plan r5, close-results and close-delta (all digests match) beside the five phase records, the shipped code paths (model_index.py, universe.py, model/_unattended.py, model/_includes.py, commands/checking.py, evolve/service.py, evolve/_includes.py, evolve/cli_service.py), the four pages and the cited VG1-VG5 tests. Every goal predicate in the plan maps to record evidence that would fail if the predicate were false; the code behaves as the records and delta say, and models without the unattended mode or without includes are unchanged on every tested path; the pages state what the code does with one home per rule; every open question raised in the records is dispositioned and no disposition is wrong; the five close amendments keep their r4 wording verbatim and are each supported by the record that raised them (verified against 002/003/004/006 and the close gates). One hardening gap survives: VG3-C7's universal byte-identical claim is evidenced only over valid sampled models, while the H17/H37 remapping shipped in VG3 changes issue paths on refused include roots that lack the unattended mode, a compatibility surface plan section 5 does not name.
